boy-scouts-in-the-coal-caverns-or-the-li: Part of G. Harvey Ralphson's long-running Boy Scouts series, this adventure sends a troop of young scouts into the dark passages of coal mines. Underground they face cave-ins, getting lost, and the test of keeping cool when danger strikes. Written for boys of the 1910s, the story mixes thrills with the movement's lessons in courage, teamwork, and quick thinking.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aix: This 1913 reference article on Aix — Aix-en-Provence, the archdiocese of southern France. Georges Goyau gives its proud history. Its cathedral keeps old Provençal glory. Councils and saints mark its past. A metropolitan see of the Midi. Its archbishops crowned no kings but ruled souls.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-crucifi: This 1913 reference piece on the altar crucifix — the cross that must face the priest. Augustin Schulte explains the law. Christ's image crowns every altar. The Mass looks to Calvary. The altar's necessary sign. Its corpus reminds the priest of Calvary.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archaeology-o: This 1913 reference piece on the archaeology of the cross and crucifix — the symbol's ancient story. Orazio Marucchi traces its earliest forms. The catacombs hid the veiled cross. Constantine's age displayed it boldly. The sign's long history in stone. Its plates show the symbol's growth.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-beatrix: This 1913 reference piece on Beatrix — a name in the saints' story. Herbert Thurston records what is known. The entry preserves her modest fame. The old calendars keep her name. A holy woman of the early Church. Her memory lives in the calendars.
